clue.text: Gervais v Wilde in mental combat?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, cryptically: Ricky Gervais and Oscar Wilde are both famous wits, so a contest between them is a clash of two clever talkers
second meaning: a contest of quick intelligence and repartee

explanation.walkthrough: Ricky Gervais is a British comedian and Oscar Wilde the Irish playwright famed for epigrams; 'v' (versus) turns the pair into a fight between wits.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names any contest where opponents try to outsmart each other through cleverness and repartee rather than force.

clue.text: Stopped up and watched, seeing Belgium oust Conservative

indicators.note: to oust is to push out and take the place of, so one letter turns out another

parts.note: to clock is informal for to notice or watch
B is the international vehicle code for Belgium
C is the standard abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: Someone watched a drain being cleared after Belgium threw out the Conservative party.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the C of CLOCKED for B to get BLOCKED.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe that is obstructed or clogged can be described as stopped up, the same past participle sense.

clue.text: Server and host finally tuck into flatfish

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word it follows, keeping only its closing letter

parts.note: the last letter of host
to tuck into food is to eat it
a ray is a flat-bodied fish

explanation.surface: A waiter and the host of a dinner tuck into a plate of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Server' looks like a person, but here it is the object you carry cups and plates on.
explanation.definitionFit: A tray carrying cups, pot and cakes is used for serving refreshments, so it is a server in that sense.

clue.text: Pride participants invented stories about one's son

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one set of letters goes around the others

parts.note: untrue stories are lies
taken as written, without the apostrophe
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Someone at a Pride event made up tales about their son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pride' suggests a parade, but it is the collective noun for a group of lions.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of lions is called a pride, and its female members are the hunters within that group.

clue.text: They play on Beethoven's overture, each section taking bows

indicators.note: a ship's bows are its front end, so taking the bows of each word means taking its opening letter

parts.note: the initial letters of these five words

explanation.surface: An orchestra plays Beethoven's overture and every section stands to take a bow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking bows' pictures applause at a concert, but it asks for the front of each word.
explanation.definitionFit: Oboes are woodwind instruments, and in an orchestra the instruments are what is played, so they are things that play.

clue.text: Women's clubs maybe welcoming French and rubber gear

indicators.note: welcoming means letting in, so the outer letters take another word inside them

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women
et is French for and; the clue's 'French and' together give it
clubs is one suit in a pack of cards, hence 'maybe'

explanation.surface: Women's clubs welcome French members and sell rubber equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clubs' suggests societies, but it is a card suit; 'French and' together supply the French word for 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: A diver's or surfer's close-fitting neoprene outfit is protective clothing made of a rubber material.

clue.text: Picked up oolong perhaps old Chinese packed

indicators.note: picked up means heard, as on a radio, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: oolong is a kind of Chinese tea; a golf tee sounds the same
the Ming were a Chinese dynasty, 1368 to 1644

explanation.surface: Someone picked up some oolong tea that an old Chinese merchant had packed.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeming means swarming or full to bursting, so a place crammed with people is packed.

clue.text: Party focusing on economy, reducing employment

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read cryptically: the Labour party concentrating on thrift
second meaning: describing a device that cuts down the work needed

explanation.walkthrough: Labour is one of Britain's two main political parties; read whole, the phrase describes an appliance that saves effort.
explanation.definitionFit: A dishwasher is a classic gadget that cuts the human work a task needs, which is to reduce the employment of effort.

clue.text: Eat this when stoned: halve once and top with odd trimmings

indicators.note: trimming away the odd-numbered letters leaves only every second one

parts.note: the even letters of this run of words

explanation.surface: A recipe step: cut it in two, then garnish with odd bits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stoned' suggests drugs, but it means with the stone removed, and halving is how you get the stone out.
explanation.definitionFit: This green fruit has one large pit which is taken out before you eat the flesh, so it is eaten stoned.

clue.text: Article probes running — become active

indicators.note: something that probes pushes its way into the middle of whatever it examines

parts.note: a machine that is running is on
the definite article
to go is to become, as in go red

explanation.surface: A newspaper article investigates a running scandal and urges readers to get involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Become active' reads as one instruction, but it splits: 'become' is wordplay and 'active' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone always busy and moving about, never resting, is described by this idiom as constantly occupied.

clue.text: Earlier train time's lost million for profitable network?

indicators.note: lost means gone missing, so the named letter is taken away

parts.note: old means of an earlier time
to school is to train or educate
taken as written
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A complaint about a railway: the old train timetable has gone, costing millions.
explanation.walkthrough: TIME loses its M to give TIE. The old school tie stands for the British habit of former pupils of elite schools helping each other.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the informal web of favours among alumni of the same private school, which brings careers and advantage.

clue.text: Start of tariffs in Korea crushed Eastern growth

indicators.note: something crushed is mangled out of shape, so the letters are jumbled
the start of a word is its first letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: the first letter of tariffs
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for Eastern

explanation.surface: The arrival of tariffs in Korea has crushed economic growth in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: T goes into KOREA and the lot is jumbled, then E is added. 'Growth' looks economic but is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree is something that grows from the soil, and this hardwood is a classic example of such vegetation.

clue.text: Investigated macho guy that is meeting daughter

parts.note: a stud is slang for a virile, macho man
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A tough guy's background is looked into when he meets his daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: To have studied a matter is to have examined it closely, which matches looking into or researching it.

clue.text: Flipping florid

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a mild British swear word, like bloody
second meaning: reddish, healthily flushed in the face

explanation.walkthrough: Both 'flipping' and the answer are mild British substitutes for 'bloody'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means red-faced or rosy in complexion, and is also a polite British intensifier used like a mild oath.

clue.text: Critical of BBC, I get art show rejected

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the letters are read in the opposite direction
of here means taken from, so the word is a part of the run of letters that follows

parts.note: a run of letters inside these words, starting with the last letter of BBC

explanation.surface: A critic of the BBC finds an arts programme turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Critical of BBC' reads like an opinion, but 'Critical' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Strategic means of crucial importance to an overall plan, so a strategic point is a critical or vital one.

clue.text: River rose, unexpectedly creating this?

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests things turning out in a surprising order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: both words taken as written

explanation.surface: A river rose without warning and formed a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and the definition: a river rising behind a dam creates a lake of stored water.
explanation.definitionFit: A reservoir is a large lake formed when a river is dammed, so the water level climbs and stores supply.

clue.text: Stars put out by censors?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: symbols that replace the letters of rude words in print

explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' sounds like censors suppressing something, but it means printed: censored swear words appear as rows of symbols.
explanation.definitionFit: These typographic symbols look like little stars, and editors print them in place of the letters of obscenities.

clue.text: Twister split, with bother to follow

parts.note: something split is torn
ado is fuss or bother

explanation.surface: A twister tore things apart, with plenty of trouble afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Twister is an informal name for a violent rotating windstorm, from the way its funnel spins.

clue.text: Again choose roll laced with a dash — rum etc

parts.note: a reel is a roll of film or thread; the dash threaded through it is the hyphen in the answer

indicators.note: rum is old British slang for odd or strange, so the letters come out in an odd order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bread roll soaked in a splash of rum and other spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'dash' is the hyphen in the answer, threaded into the roll after its first two letters; 'rum' is the anagram signal, not the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-elect is to vote someone back into office for another term, choosing them once more.

clue.text: Staff try tropical food

parts.note: to man a post is to staff it
a go is an attempt or try

explanation.surface: Workers sample some exotic dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: The mango is a sweet fruit grown in hot climates, so it is an edible crop of the tropics.

clue.text: Robot possibly in a state, getting cold then hot internally

indicators.note: internally means on the inside, so these letters are placed within the other word

parts.note: Maine is a US state
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

explanation.surface: A robot gets into a state, running cold and then overheating inside.
explanation.walkthrough: C then H go inside MAINE. 'In a state' looks like agitation, but it names a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: A robot is one example of a mechanical device built to do work automatically, hence 'possibly'.

clue.text: Pint? Definitely!

definitions.meaning: first meaning, cryptically: a full pint is not a half-pint
second meaning: British slang for an emphatic yes

explanation.walkthrough: In British pubs beer comes in pints and halves; the reply also sounds like someone eagerly accepting a pint.
explanation.definitionFit: In British speech this phrase is an enthusiastic yes, meaning very much so or absolutely.

clue.text: Shakespearean king's visiting Italy twice over from another Med country

indicators.note: turned over means flipped end to end, so the whole is read backwards
a visitor goes inside a place, so this word sits within the others

parts.note: I is the vehicle code for Italy, used twice
King Lear is Shakespeare's tragic king, with the possessive s

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean king visits Italy twice, coming from another Mediterranean land.
explanation.walkthrough: LEAR'S goes between two Is, and the result is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Israel lies on the eastern Mediterranean coast, so a person or thing from there is Israeli.

clue.text: Paint pa's dropped or spilled, opening

indicators.note: dropped means let go of, so those letters are removed from the word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, without the possessive

indicators.note: anything spilled is scattered in a mess, so the letters land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Dad has dropped or spilled the paint just as he opened the tin.
explanation.walkthrough: PAINT without PA leaves INT; add OR and jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is short for an introduction, the opening section of a song, book or speech.

clue.text: Some cartwheeling fool at ice rink show

indicators.note: a cartwheel turns the body head over heels, so the letters are read backwards
some means a part of, so the word is a portion of the run of letters

parts.note: a run of letters spanning these words

explanation.surface: A clown turns cartwheels during a show on the ice.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a performance, typically of music or poetry, given to an audience, so it is a show.

clue.text: Most dignified resting place required by saint

parts.note: a grave is a final resting place
St is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A dignified burial plot is wanted for a saint.
explanation.definitionFit: Grave means solemn and serious, so the superlative form describes the most solemn or weighty manner.

clue.text: Original, 20, friend in Paris producing Japanese art

indicators.note: the cross-reference to the answer at 20 means not half, so only half the word is kept

parts.note: taken as written
ami is French for friend

explanation.surface: An original French friend produces a piece of Japanese art.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer at 20 is NOT HALF, so 'Original' loses half its letters to give ORIG.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the traditional craft from Japan of folding paper into decorative figures.

clue.text: Prepare tediously for amateur production

indicators.note: to prepare something is to make it ready by working it over, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: both words taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone gets ready, slowly and boringly, for a homemade show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prepare' looks like part of the surface's verb phrase but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: DIY is home improvement work done without hiring professionals, so it is the output of unpaid hobbyists.
